programs.description: Hypoxia-inducible genes promoting angiogenesis and vascular remodeling in glioblastoma. VEGFA, ANGPTL4, and SERPINE1 are canonical hypoxia-response genes upregulated under low oxygen conditions. APLN acts through APLNR to promote tumor angiogenesis, while NDRG1 is a stress-responsive protein induced by hypoxia. These genes collectively drive neovascularization to support tumor growth.

citation.reference: Investigating Glioblastoma Response to Hypoxia. Biomedicines 2020
citation.notes: VEGFA, ANGPTL4, and SERPINE1 upregulated during hypoxia in glioblastoma

citation.reference: Hypoxia upregulates the expression of the NDRG1 gene. BMC Cancer 2004
citation.notes: NDRG1 induced by hypoxia in multiple cancers

predicted_cellular_impact: Enhanced tumor vascularization and perfusion
Increased glioma cell survival under hypoxic stress
Promotion of therapy resistance through improved oxygen/nutrient delivery
Facilitation of tumor invasion via vascular co-option
programs.evidence_summary: VEGFA, ANGPTL4, and SERPINE1 are strongly upregulated in hypoxic glioblastoma and correlate with poor prognosis. APLN/APLNR signaling controls angiogenesis-dependent GBM growth. NDRG1 is hypoxia-induced and associated with chemoresistance.

citations.reference: Investigating Glioblastoma Response to Hypoxia. Biomedicines 2020
Apelin Controls Angiogenesis-Dependent Glioblastoma Growth. Int J Mol Sci 2020
ANGPTL4 Induces TMZ Resistance of Glioblastoma. Int J Mol Sci 2019

programs.description: Coordinated expression of collagen family members and fibronectin that regulate extracellular matrix composition and biomechanical properties. COL1A2, COL5A1, and COL6A2 contribute to ECM stiffness, promoting glioma invasion and immunosuppression. FN1 supports cell adhesion and migration. Increased ECM stiffness correlates with glioblastoma progression and poor prognosis.

citation.reference: COL6A2: A Key Survival-Related Gene. Cancer Manag Res 2025
citation.notes: COL6A2 promotes GBM proliferation, invasion, and immunosuppression

citation.reference: Physics of Brain Cancer: ECM Stiffening. Cancers 2022

predicted_cellular_impact: Increased tumor tissue stiffness promoting invasion
Enhanced immune evasion through ECM barrier formation
Promotion of mesenchymal transition
Support for therapy resistance
programs.evidence_summary: COL1A2, COL5A1, COL6A2 are upregulated in high-grade glioma and associated with poor prognosis. COL6A2 specifically promotes chemoresistance and immunosuppression. ECM stiffness is a critical regulator of glioblastoma malignancy.

citations.reference: COL6A2: A Key Survival-Related Gene Restricting Antitumor Immunity in Glioblastoma
Microenvironmental stiffness induces metabolic reprogramming in glioblastoma. Cell Rep 2023

programs.description: CHI3L1 (YKL-40) orchestrates multiple immunosuppressive mechanisms in glioblastoma. It drives M2 macrophage polarization via CD44 interaction and AKT pathway activation, promotes vascular mimicry in glioma stem cells, and correlates with immune checkpoint expression (CD274/PD-L1). CHI3L1 also activates NF-κB signaling in tumor cells and reprograms the tumor microenvironment to an immunosuppressive phenotype.

citation.reference: Chitinase-3-like-1 protein complexes modulate macrophage-mediated immune suppression. J Clin Invest 2021
citation.notes: CHI3L1 binding with Galectin-3 promotes M2 TAM infiltration

citation.reference: Chitinase-3 like-protein-1 promotes glioma via NF-κB and TME reprogramming. Theranostics 2022

predicted_cellular_impact: Recruitment and M2 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages
Upregulation of immune checkpoint molecules (PD-L1, LAG3)
Creation of immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment
Enhancement of glioma stem cell properties via angiogenesis/vasculogenic mimicry
programs.evidence_summary: CHI3L1 is highly expressed in mesenchymal GBM and correlates with poor prognosis. It physically interacts with Galectin-3 to selectively recruit M2-like TAMs. CHI3L1 also activates kynurenine pathway metabolism to establish immunosuppressive microenvironment.

citations.reference: Chitinase-3-like-1 protein complexes modulate macrophage-mediated immune suppression in glioblastoma. J Clin Invest 2021

programs.description: Expression of immune checkpoint molecules CD274 (PD-L1) that inhibit T cell activation and promote immune escape. PD-L1 expression in glioblastoma induces and maintains regulatory T cells (Tregs) and is associated with immunosuppressive M2 macrophages. High PD-L1 expression correlates with therapy resistance and poor outcomes.

atomic_biological_processes.name: negative regulation of T cell activation

Reduced efficacy of immunotherapy
programs.evidence_summary: PD-L1 is expressed in 61-88% of glioblastomas. PD-L1+ myeloid cells are associated with increased Treg abundance. PD-L1 expression correlates with M2 macrophage infiltration and radioresistance.

citations.reference: The immune checkpoint protein PD-L1 induces and maintains regulatory T cells. Oncoimmunology 2018

programs.description: IDO1 catalyzes tryptophan degradation to kynurenine, creating an immunosuppressive microenvironment through both enzymatic and non-enzymatic mechanisms. IDO1 is expressed in >90% of glioblastomas and suppresses anti-tumor immunity via tryptophan depletion, kynurenine accumulation, and upregulation of complement factor H (CFH). Both enzymatic and non-canonical IDO1 functions contribute to immune suppression.

citation.reference: Tumor Cell IDO Enhances Immune Suppression Independent of Tryptophan Metabolism. Clin Cancer Res 2021

atomic_biological_processes.name: negative regulation of T cell mediated immunity

citation.reference: Tryptophan Metabolism Contributes to Radiation-Induced Immune Checkpoint Reactivation. Clin Cancer Res 2018

predicted_cellular_impact: Depletion of tryptophan from tumor microenvironment
Accumulation of immunosuppressive kynurenine metabolites
Suppression of effector T cell function
Upregulation of complement inhibitors (CFH)
Promotion of regulatory T cell expansion
programs.evidence_summary: IDO1 is expressed in >90% of GBM and correlates with poor survival. Non-enzymatic IDO1 activity increases CFH expression independent of tryptophan metabolism. IDO1 also promotes angiogenesis via GCN2 pathway activation and VEGFA upregulation.

citations.reference: Tumor Cell IDO Enhances Immune Suppression and Decreases Survival Independent of Tryptophan Metabolism. Clin Cancer Res 2021

programs.description: SPP1 (osteopontin) promotes glioblastoma invasion, migration, and stem cell self-renewal. It mediates macrophage recruitment and M2 polarization via integrin αvβ5 and CD44 receptors. SPP1 is overexpressed in glioma-initiating cells and regulated by GLI1 and OCT4, linking it to stemness pathways. Expression correlates with glioma grade and macrophage infiltration.

programs.description: MET receptor tyrosine kinase activation drives epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, invasion, and therapy resistance in glioblastoma. MET promotes mesenchymal transition and scattered cell phenotype, contributing to therapy resistance.

programs.description: IL4R (interleukin-4 receptor) signaling promotes M2 macrophage polarization, creating an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. IL-4 and IL-13 both signal through the shared IL-4Rα subunit to drive M2 phenotype characterized by increased CD206 expression. M2 macrophages suppress anti-tumor immunity and promote glioblastoma progression.

programs.description: FOSL1 (FRA-1), a component of AP-1 transcription factor, drives proneural-to-mesenchymal transition of glioma stem cells and promotes proliferation, invasion, and stemness. programs.description: BIRC3 (cIAP2) is an inhibitor of apoptosis protein that promotes therapy resistance and stemness in glioblastoma. BIRC3 is upregulated in response to radiation and temozolomide treatment via STAT3 and PI3K signaling. It is essential for senescent GBM cell survival after therapy and promotes stemness reprogramming. BIRC3 is a biomarker of mesenchymal and hypoxia-driven GBM habitats.

predicted_cellular_impact: Evasion of therapy-induced apoptosis

Facilitation of tumor recurrence after treatment
programs.evidence_summary: BIRC3 is the only IAP whose expression is associated with long-term survival in GBM. BIRC3 expression increases with recurrence and is upregulated by RT/TMZ via STAT3/PI3K. Senescent GBM cells upregulate BIRC3 and rely on it for survival. BIRC3 drives stemness reprogramming and is a biomarker of mesenchymal/hypoxic GBM.

HMGA2 regulates let-7 microRNA pathway and activates MMP2 transcription via chromatin remodeling to promote invasion.

programs.description: PROM1 (CD133) is a widely used marker for glioma stem cells and is associated with poor prognosis in glioblastoma. MTAP loss promotes PROM1 expression via hypomethylation.

GBP5 has been shown to drive malignancy via Src/ERK1/2/MMP3 pathway in mesenchymal GBM.
